format.audio: MP3 (LAME VBR, with the LAME header that makes decoders drop the encoder padding), 44.1 kHz
format.lead: 0: after decodeAudioData the note starts at sample 0 of the buffer (measured in Chromium)
format.gain: dB to apply to the instrument or kit so that all of them are equally loud (-21 LUFS for a loud mid-range note, kits -27 LUFS for a loud snare); never above 0, so one note cannot clip: add your own master gain
format.vel: nominal velocity of the dynamic layer (50 = soft, 100 = loud): pick the layer nearest to the played velocity, then scale its level for the velocities in between
format.loop: instrument "loop": true means its samples carry "loopStart" and "loopEnd" (seconds into the decoded file): set source.loop = true, source.loopStart, source.loopEnd and stop the note with a gain ramp of "release" seconds. A sample without them is a one-shot. Ignoring the loop points is safe: every file ends with a fade.
format.range: MIDI notes the instrument is meant to play; no note in it is more than 3 semitones from a sample of every layer
format.kits: "pieces" holds the loud hits (round robins: play them in turn or at random); "layers" optionally adds a soft layer (vel 50) per piece; "absent" lists contract pieces a kit does not have
